div.div: Same work, more cycles: in the full stack fixed-work threads run the same instructions with 1.4× to 2× the cycles [cycles_growth_range, illustrative]; moving the motor-control services' cluster-mates removes about two thirds of the extra cycles (class "most (or less board traffic)")

Alone -> full stack, user-mode counts per fixed work unit (one bus cycle / one audio message / one detector frame), three fixed-work threads. Ratio to alone; the full-stack bar spans the range over the threads. Pre-registered class: X2 "slower work" for all three.
ratio to alone (alone = 1×)
1× (growth 0.0) [instr_growth, illustrative]

instructions per unit
left alone, right full stack
1.4×–2× [cycles_growth_range]

cycles per unit
left alone, right full stack
0.5×–0.7× (drop 0.3–0.5) [ipc_drop_range, illustrative]

IPC
left alone, right full stack
2×–3× [l3_refill_ratio_range, illustrative]

L3 refills per instruction (a hint, not a cause)
left alone, right full stack

Clock unchanged (all cores locked). The motor loop is never preempted, so its slowdown is not run-queue wait. Kernel-mode instructions do rise for some threads; message fan-out, interrupt and scheduler work are not separated. My estimate: full-stack ratio = 1 + growth, IPC = 1 − drop.

Cluster move: every service sharing the motor-control services' CPU cluster goes to the pool. X = the motor loop's user cycles per bus cycle; two arms, "baseline" (full stack) and "moved", two windows each.
X_alone
X_moved
X_base
full-stack growth X_base − X_alone
removed X_base − X_moved
schematic: bar lengths show only the ratio f, not cycle counts
"part" = predicted before the run
"most (or less board traffic)"
f = 0.65 [cluster_move_recovered, illustrative], close to the line
removed fraction f = (X_base − X_moved) ÷ (X_base − X_alone); dashed line = pre-registered class line 0.5 [cluster_move_class_line, illustrative]

Prediction failed; the path stays open. Predicted "part"; f lands above the line, so read it as "about two thirds", not a clean "most". (1) The two moved windows differ, and the spread reaches toward the line. (2) Board memory traffic fell in the moved arm, so the class carries "(or less board traffic)". (3) The motor-control services' own load also fell. The other ~0.35 is not separated (my estimate from `cluster_move_recovered`: 1 − 0.65).

The move is not a free fix. The moved services land on the pool: the camera loses 4 to 6 Hz [cluster_move_camera_cost_hz, illustrative]; other pool services and message delay get worse.
Earlier cache A/B: a synthetic L3-footprint load on the neighbouring cores reproduced a slower motor loop; an L1-resident load reproduced nothing.

Legend
left: grey bar = alone (1×); coloured bar = full stack, solid to the low end of the range and dashed outline to the high end; thick dark-blue border = IPC; dashed horizontal line = alone level.
right: grey = alone, mid-blue = baseline, light blue dashed = moved; dot = f; dashed outline / dashed line = the prediction and the pre-registered class line.
purple dashed box = why the result is not a clean cause; amber = the cost of the fix.

Sources. Numbers loaded from ../constants.json by spec04.py; key in brackets. Note A2 (counters, cluster move, cache A/B). The cache mechanism is taught in ../../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/notes/B2-cache-level-interference.md.
Illustrative (round teaching numbers that keep the shape of a finding; not measurements): cycles_growth_range, instr_growth, ipc_drop_range, l3_refill_ratio_range, cluster_move_recovered, cluster_move_class_line, cluster_move_camera_cost_hz.
